where: the whole read-only page — the 'Signed-in team 11' card ends at x=1024, and the 384px column from x=1024 to the container edge at x=1408 is empty; there is no Invited section anywhere in the markup
finding: A core member's stated job is 'who is on the team and who has never signed in.' The read-only page answers the first half for eleven people and silently drops four more. Hannah Boateng gets an amber 'Never signed in' badge because she has a profile; ken.tanaka@example.org — invited to Core team six days ago and equally never signed in — does not exist on this screen at all. The core member leaves with a headcount of eleven when four addresses can already sign in, and cannot answer the question they most plausibly came with ('did Ken ever accept?') without asking an admin. The page's own disclosure makes this worse: open 'How Tally decides who may sign in' and it explains that 'an admin invites somebody here, they sign in with that Google account, and their profile appears beside this' — the page names the pending state and then never shows it. The card title 'Signed-in team' is honest, but honest-and-incomplete on a screen with nothing else on it is still a wrong answer.
evidence: team-core--desktop.html contains zero occurrences of 'Invited' / 'invited'. Card measured at x=255–1024, y=155–815; the void to its right is 384px wide and 660px tall — exactly the 24rem the admin's invite column occupies in team--desktop-fold.png, where the same four invitations (rosa 2 days, ken 6 days, wednesday.volunteer suspended 24 days, noor 40 minutes) all fit above the fold with 14px to spare. So the missing information costs nothing to display: it is already proven to fit in that column at this viewport, and 85px of vertical slack remains under the roster card as well.
direction: Give the read-only page the admin's two-column page grid (`lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_24rem]`) and put a controls-free Invited card in it: header, count badge, the address, the role granted and 'invited N days ago', and the exception badge for the suspended one — no form, no Withdraw, no checkbox. Keep the 768px cap on the roster card so round 2's identity-cell fix survives. If product has decided pending invitations are admin-only information, then the constraint blocks the card and the fix becomes one line of text under the roster count ('4 more have been invited and have not signed in yet') so the core member at least knows the category exists.

where: the meta line of each invitation row in the Invited card, right column, y=508 / 613 / 719 / 826
finding: The role an invitation grants is the most consequential fact in that column, and it is set in the faintest ink on the page inside a run-on sentence. 'Core team · invited 6 days ago' under ken.tanaka is a pending elevation of access to a roster of minors, rendered identically to 'Counselor · invited 2 days ago'. The admin auditing elevated access has just been taught, four inches to the left, that elevated roles wear a brand ring — Grace Kim and Miriam Achebe both carry a 'Core team' pill on the admin frame's role column, and Marcus's exception is a red badge. The Invited card uses none of that vocabulary, so at a glance it reads as four uniform counselor invites with one red flag, and the pending core grant hides in the grey. Round 2's rationale for leaving this line at ink-500 said it was '14px reference prose, not the 12px cited failure' — the markup says `text-xs text-ink-500`, so it is 12px, and it measures 3.75:1 against the card, while the member emails right beside it were raised to 6.96:1 in the same round.
evidence:
Sampled from team--desktop-fold.png: invitation meta line fg rgb(100,116,139) on rgb(15,23,42) = 3.75:1 at 12px (fails AA for small text); member email fg rgb(148,163,184) = 6.96:1; recency = 12.02:1. Markup: `

Core team · invited 6 days ago

`.
direction: Apply the round-2 lane rule to the second list too: pull the granted role out of the sentence and render it with the same token the roster uses — ring badge for Core team / Admin, plain text for Counselor — leaving 'invited 6 days ago' as the only thing on the meta line, and step that line to ink-400 to match the addresses it sits under. One vocabulary for 'this person has elevated access', whether they have signed in yet or not.

where: the recency column of both roster tables, x=558 (admin) / x=703 (read-only), all eleven rows
finding: This is the verdict on the header row round 2 deferred: I would not build it now. The argument for it was space, and space is no longer scarce — both pages fit the fold with the admin frame using y=25 to y=886 of 900 and the read-only page ending at y=815. What remains is the repetition: 'Last seen ' consumes roughly 62px of a 168px column eleven times over. But because the prefix is constant-width, the values stay left-aligned to each other at a fixed offset, so the eye can fixate past it and read only the varying tail — the scan cost is close to zero. A header row would buy back ink the page does not need and would cost two new label sets (Role/Access on the admin grid, none on the read-only one) plus a responsive prefix below `@2xl`, which is a lot of structure for a cosmetic gain on a page that no longer scrolls.
evidence: Row pitch measured at 53px from the dividers in team--desktop-fold.png (y=291, 344, 397 … 821); recency column 10.5rem = 168px, 'Last seen ' occupies x=558–620. Eleven rows, no scroll, on both frames.
direction: Drop the deferred header row from the backlog, or take only its cheap half if the repetition still bothers: keep the column as-is and leave it alone. Do not spend a round on it.
